name: Seth Blitzspear
caption: A former World WAR! Champion and the fed's own longest-running headliner, feuding with the Masters of War stable from the fed's own first weeks and still main-eventing a year and a half later.

tenures.role: wrestler — former World WAR! Champion; leader of WAR!Force
tenures.source: The fed's own founding-era Masters of War feud (msg_id l7hCo0slp3IJ); numerous WarZone/WAR!fare show scripts through the fed's own Tournament of Champions (msg_id znndSz3YbaMJ, 30 Oct 1996).

name: "The Reverend" J.R. Death
caption: A 7'6" powerhouse who held the World WAR! Championship through the fed's own Oct 1995-Feb 1996 season, retaining it against Seth Blitzspear on "World WAR! III," and briefly the International WAR! Championship the same autumn.

tenures.source: "WarZone 3" (msg_id GBLrIOyPOnAJ, 20 Oct 1995); "Masters of War 3" (msg_id Dg-tAnaiLnQJ, 22 Oct 1995, no world-title match "because Randy Blake gets a break" — implying Blake's own prior reign); "World WAR! III" (msg_id JCaUjV3tCqMJ, 5 Feb 1996), where Vice-President Helmroy orders Death to defend against Blitzspear and Death retains.

name: "The Economist" Randy Blake
caption: An early World WAR! Champion and recurring mentor figure, later managing and training Booster Dunne to the International title.

tenures.source: A community continuity thread names Blake the winner of the World WAR!/FWAR! interfed title at "Casualties of WAR!" (cited in msg_id 40DULtDg4JYJ, 2 Jul 1995); confirmed still champion, resting, at "Masters of War 3" (msg_id Dg-tAnaiLnQJ). Later recurring as Booster Dunne's cornerman through the fed's own May 1996 WAR!fare broadcasts and the Oct 1996 Tournament of Champions.

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (randy-blake-svw); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

name: Tonnage
caption: A 565-pound member of the Armageddon stable who won the World WAR! Championship from Stein "Ice" Berg at WARATHON I, retaining it into that May before an off-page loss the fed's own record does not otherwise document.

tenures.role: wrestler — multiple-time World WAR! Champion; Armageddon
tenures.source: "WarZone 3" and "Masters of War 3" (Oct 1995, undercard); won the World WAR! title from Stein "Ice" Berg at WARATHON 1 (recapped in "The WAR! Report," msg_id BliXg_NDnrAJ, 29 Apr 1996); defended successfully through "Tuesday Night WAR!fare" and "Monday Night WAR!fare" (May 1996); by the Oct 1996 Tournament of Champions round read here he is again pursuing the title rather than holding it (msg_id znndSz3YbaMJ), an off-page loss this pull does not otherwise document; reported retiring soon per "Nuclear WAR!fare" (msg_id EwViELllpWQJ, 7 Dec 1996).

name: Jerry "Goon" Gordon
caption: A fan-favorite "Michigan State Spartan" who briefly held two titles at once in the fed's own early run and remained a top babyface through 1996.

tenures.source: "Masters of War 3" (msg_id Dg-tAnaiLnQJ): wins the Liberty title from The Mandarin, "the first person to have ever held two titles in WAR!"; recurring through "Tuesday Night WAR!fare," "Wednesday Night WAR!fare" and "Nuclear WAR!fare."

name: Booster Dunne
caption: "The Blue and Gold," an International WAR! Champion whose classic title defense against Lord Byron on "Monday Night WAR!fare" is rated a match-of-the-year candidate in the show's own text.

tenures.source: "WarZone 3" (undercard, Oct 1995); champion by "Tuesday Night WAR!fare" (msg_id 1V1AqI0LVRcJ, 6 May 1996), retaining there against Johnny Dreamer (non-title) and at "Monday Night WAR!fare" (msg_id Dp_4KLyWHg8J, 13 May 1996) against Lord Byron; no longer champion by "Wednesday Night WAR!fare" (16 Oct 1996), where Butch Williams defends the belt instead — the title change between these two shows is not in the held record.

name: OG Gary Trent
caption: A founding-era Compton, California wrestler ("Original Gangsta" Gary Trent) who feuded with WAR!'s own early heels and later challenged for the Liberty title.

tenures.source: "[WAR!] The OG Gary Trent" (msg_id xI1s-e_z6MQJ, 4 Jun 1995); recurring through "WarZone 3," "Masters of War 3," and a Liberty title challenge against DeathJester on "Monday Night WAR!fare" (13 May 1996).

name: Sid "StrayCat" Starr
caption: A self-described "coolest thing in the ring," billed on his debut as a reigning CWWW champion, who won and lost the WAR! Liberty Championship in the fed's own Season 2 title scramble before recurring as a cheating heel through 1996.

tenures.source: "WarZone 3" (msg_id GBLrIOyPOnAJ, 20 Oct 1995), billed "the current CWWW North American & Internet Champion"; recurring through "Superstars At War! I," "Monday Night WAR!fare," and the Oct 1996 Tournament of Champions cluster.
Won the Living Legends Cup's own second first-round match over Tommy Danger with a hidden pair of brass knuckles.

The promotion's own served Update 1.1 (original roster, a heel) and Fusion 1.2 (beats debuting Laramee); the RSPWF Top 200's own 2004 #8 placing tags this same wrestler WILD. This record already carries a presumed-same identity edge to sid-starr-war-1995 ("Sid 'StrayCat' Starr"), unaffected here.

name: Stein "Ice" Berg
caption: A 430-pound Norwegian brawler and former World WAR! Champion, later a recurring member of Armageddon's rival stable, WAR!Force.

tenures.source: Recurring from "Superstars At War! I" (Feb 1996); lost the World WAR! title to Tonnage at WARATHON 1 (recapped, "The WAR! Report," 29 Apr 1996); recurring through "Nuclear WAR!fare" (7 Dec 1996).

name: Big Duke
caption: A recurring WAR!Lord Champion aligned with the Rich Boys stable, whose contractual disputes with the fed's own front office are a running plot thread through late 1996.

tenures.source: Recurring from "Masters of War 3" (Oct 1995, undercard) as a challenger and (per his own words on "Tuesday Night WAR!fare," msg_id 1V1AqI0LVRcJ) a former WAR!Lord Champion; loses the WAR!Lord rematch to CrocMaster on that same broadcast; his own "loser leaves town" contract dispute over the belt continues into "Nuclear WAR!fare" (7 Dec 1996).

name: CrocMaster
caption: The WAR!Lord Champion through mid-1996, defending the title against Big Duke in a bloody no-DQ rematch on "Tuesday Night WAR!fare."

tenures.source: "Tuesday Night WAR!fare" (msg_id 1V1AqI0LVRcJ, 6 May 1996): retains the WAR!Lord title against Big Duke in a no-DQ, no-countout rematch.

name: Lord Byron
caption: An English "technical wrestler" heel managed by King Benny, whose finisher (the Aristoclutch) headlines two of the fed's own title matches read here.

tenures.source: Recurring from "Masters of War 3" (Oct 1995, undercard); challenges Booster Dunne for the International WAR! title on "Monday Night WAR!fare" (13 May 1996) in a match the show's own text rates a title candidate for match of the year.

tenures.note: Challenges Gabriel Whitecross for a EMWC World Heavyweight Championship billed at this event; the served text does not resolve the finish cleanly (a contested Tony Starks angle intervenes). One month after this record's own EMWC debut.

name: DeathJester
caption: A cheating heel who won the WAR! Liberty Championship twice under two different ring names — first as Joey the Clown in the fed's own Season 2 title scramble, then reclaiming it as DeathJester in 1996 and retaining it against OG Gary Trent.

tenures.source: Champion by "The WAR! Report" (29 Apr 1996); retains against Brett Stevens (non-title, "Tuesday Night WAR!fare") and Gary Trent ("Monday Night WAR!fare," 13 May 1996).

name: American Patriot
caption: A flag-waving babyface who challenged for the World WAR! Championship and later held, then lost, the WAR!Lord Championship to Robski in a cage match.

tenures.source: Challenges Tonnage for the World WAR! title (non-finish) on "Monday Night WAR!fare" (13 May 1996); WAR!Lord Champion by "Nuclear WAR!fare" (7 Dec 1996), where he loses the belt back to Robski in a cage match.
/promotions/raw-ewu-2000/archive/let-me-tell-you-something-607-2002-01-05.html

identity.note: "American Patriot"/flag-gimmick babyfaces are a stock 1990s-e-fed archetype; four unrelated existing records share the name (american-patriot-icbinr, american-patriot-aicw, american-patriot-apw, american-patriot-twf) across different feds and eras with no shared operator, roster or date evidence -- a name-only match is not a join.

name: "Magnum" Biff McGriff
caption: A member of the Armageddon stable and International WAR! Champion from Oct 1996, who won the belt off a slow-count pinfall against Butch Williams.

tenures.source: Recurring from "Tuesday Night WAR!fare" (undercard); wins the International WAR! title from Butch Williams by pinfall on "Wednesday Night WAR!fare" (16 Oct 1996); still champion through "Nuclear WAR!fare" (7 Dec 1996), where his own I Quit title defense against Nomad ends in chaos before a finish.

name: Butch Williams
caption: "The American," later billed "The Exorcist," a two-time International WAR! Champion who also won, then immediately signed away, the Liberty Championship on his own retirement night, before losing the International belt for good to Biff McGriff on a controversial slow count.

tenures.source: Recurring from "Superstars At War! I" (Feb 1996, cage-match undercard); International WAR! Champion by "Wednesday Night WAR!fare" (16 Oct 1996), losing the title there to Biff McGriff.

name: "The Living Law" Brutus Judd
caption: A vigilante-themed brawler feuding with Armageddon, whose "Monday Night WAR!fare" match against Biff McGriff was interrupted by a flamethrower attack on a third party.

tenures.source: "Monday Night WAR!fare" (msg_id Dp_4KLyWHg8J, 13 May 1996): a no-contest against "Magnum" Biff McGriff after Suna Gib's ringside flamethrower attack on Colt McGraw.

name: "Dirty" Doug Simpkins
caption: A WAR! Liberty Champion through late 1996, retaining the belt in a finisher-vs-finisher match against Jim Bondo on "Nuclear WAR!fare."

tenures.source: Named a Liberty title challenger on "Wednesday Night WAR!fare" (16 Oct 1996); champion by "Nuclear WAR!fare" (7 Dec 1996), retaining by pinfall against Jim Bondo.

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (dirty-doug-simpkins-rspwf); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

name: Jason Midnight
caption: A World WAR! Champion crowned via a separate interfed (UWC) tournament victory, retaining the belt against Tyler Stevens in a no-DQ match on "Nuclear WAR!fare."

tenures.source: "Nuclear WAR!fare" (msg_id jToltgTggKgJ/EwViELllpWQJ, 7 Dec 1996): referenced in the broadcast's own dialogue as "newly crowned WAR! AND UWC champion" after "that big UWC interfed tournament"; retains the title in a no-DQ, no-countout match against Tyler Stevens. The originating title-change document is not in the held record.

name: Toxic Shock
caption: "Tox," the fed's own backstage interviewer and, from Feb 1996, co-host — WAR!'s own in-fiction interview-segment character, not an acronym.

tenures.source: Debuts as co-host on "World WAR! III" (msg_id JCaUjV3tCqMJ, 5 Feb 1996). Recurring backstage interviewer through "Nuclear WAR!fare" (7 Dec 1996). This corroborates the finding that "Tox"/"Toxic Shock" is WAR!'s own in-fiction interview-segment character, not an acronym.

identity.note: An unrelated existing character, toxic-shock-giwf (GIWF), shares the gimmick name with no shared operator, roster or date evidence connecting the two feds -- a name-only match is not a join.

name: Jacob "Jake" Kane
caption: WAR!'s own founder and lead fedhead, credited on the fed's own broadcasts throughout this pull and, per an existing museum ruling, "the legendary mastermind of WAR! and E-wrestling University."

tenures.source: Signs the fed's own founding-era posts (e.g. msg_id TwjSTueEhvMJ, 13 Oct 1995, "Jacob 'jake' Kane & the pHantom ahh fan club"); credited on the "WAR! Fedheads" footer of "Wednesday Night WAR!fare" (16 Oct 1996) and the Tournament of Champions distribution header (30 Oct 1996).

name: "Avocado" Bob Whitely
caption: WAR!'s own lead play-by-play commentator across nearly the whole run read here, from the Oct 1995 relaunch through the Dec 1996 supercard.

tenures.source: "WarZone 3" (Oct 1995) through "Nuclear WAR!fare" (7 Dec 1996), where he returns as senior match-commentator after a period off-air.

name: "Bullfrog" Eric Helmroy
caption: WAR!'s own color commentator and, in-fiction, Vice-President — the authority figure who rules on title stipulations and roster discipline throughout the read shows.

tenures.role: commentator — also WAR!'s own in-fiction Vice-President, ruling on stipulations and discipline
tenures.source: "WarZone 3" (Oct 1995) as co-host and self-described Vice-President; rules on the World WAR! title stipulation on "World WAR! III" (5 Feb 1996) and bans Seth Blitzspear from title contention there; recurring through "Monday Night WAR!fare" (13 May 1996).

name: Tony Taylor
caption: A play-by-play announcer who anchored the fed's own "WAR! Report" news broadcast and several 1996 WAR!fare cards opposite "Terrible" Terry James.

tenures.source: "The WAR! Report" (29 Apr 1996) through "Tuesday Night WAR!fare" and "Monday Night WAR!fare" (May 1996).

name: "Terrible" Terry James
caption: A brash, self-promoting color commentator (and, by his own account, a onetime GIWF manager) who anchored most of the fed's own 1996 broadcasts read in this pull.

tenures.source: "Tuesday Night WAR!fare" (6 May 1996) through "Nuclear WAR!fare" (7 Dec 1996).

name: Robski
caption: A heel wrestler embroiled in a running contract dispute with Big Duke over the WAR!Lord title, who regains the belt from American Patriot in a cage match at "Nuclear WAR!fare."

tenures.source: Referenced as released from WAR! by contract dispute on the Tournament of Champions round (30 Oct 1996, beaten by Tonnage); reinstated on a technicality and regains the WAR!Lord title from American Patriot in a cage match at "Nuclear WAR!fare" (7 Dec 1996).

identity.note: An unrelated existing character, dwo-1996-robski, shares the name with no shared operator, roster or date evidence connecting the two feds -- a name-only match is not a join.

name: Zeus
caption: One half of the Divine Alliance tag team, unmasked (with Amon Ra) as "Tut and Agamemnon" after a surprise tag-title win over Canadian Carnage.

tenures.source: "WarZone 3"/"Masters of War 3" (Oct 1995); "World WAR! III" (5 Feb 1996), unmasking as half of the surprise challengers who win the World WAR! Tag Team titles.

name: Amon Ra
caption: One half of the Divine Alliance tag team, unmasked (with Zeus) as "Tut and Agamemnon" after a surprise tag-title win over Canadian Carnage.

tenures.source: "WarZone 3"/"Masters of War 3" (Oct 1995); "World WAR! III" (5 Feb 1996).

name: Big Daddy Vicelord
caption: One half of the Ghetto Boyz tag team, a recurring World WAR! Tag Team title contender through the fed's own 1996 run.

tenures.source: "Masters of War 3" (Oct 1995) through "Tuesday Night WAR!fare" (6 May 1996).

name: Folk Curtis Fredrick
caption: One half of the Ghetto Boyz tag team, a recurring World WAR! Tag Team title contender through the fed's own 1996 run.

tenures.source: "Masters of War 3" (Oct 1995) through "Tuesday Night WAR!fare" (6 May 1996).

name: Bounty Hunter
caption: One half of the Brotherhood tag team, World WAR! Tag Team Champion as of "Tuesday Night WAR!fare."

tenures.role: wrestler — the Brotherhood; World WAR! Tag Team Champion
tenures.source: "The WAR! Report" (29 Apr 1996) recap through "Tuesday Night WAR!fare" (6 May 1996), retaining the World WAR! Tag Team titles by double disqualification.

identity.note: Two unrelated existing characters (bounty-hunter-jwa-ajfa, bounty-hunter-cswa) share the stock bounty-hunter gimmick name with no shared operator, roster or date evidence -- a name-only match is not a join.

name: Bruiser Buggelli
caption: One half of the Brotherhood tag team, World WAR! Tag Team Champion as of "Tuesday Night WAR!fare."

tenures.role: wrestler — the Brotherhood; World WAR! Tag Team Champion
tenures.source: "The WAR! Report" (29 Apr 1996) recap through "Tuesday Night WAR!fare" (6 May 1996).

name: Henry Roome
caption: One half of the Star Smashers tag team, World WAR! Tag Team Champion through mid-May 1996 before losing the belts to the Aderondac Brothers.

tenures.role: wrestler — Star Smashers; former World WAR! Tag Team Champion
tenures.source: "Tuesday Night WAR!fare" (undercard win over Apocalypse) through "Monday Night WAR!fare" (13 May 1996), losing the World WAR! Tag Team titles there.

name: Apollo Friday
caption: One half of the Star Smashers tag team, World WAR! Tag Team Champion through mid-May 1996 before losing the belts to the Aderondac Brothers.

tenures.role: wrestler — Star Smashers; former World WAR! Tag Team Champion
tenures.source: "Tuesday Night WAR!fare" through "Monday Night WAR!fare" (13 May 1996).

name: Hakeem "The Machine" Owlstine
caption: One half of Industrial Revolution, World WAR! Tag Team Champion by Dec 1996, losing the belts to the Annihilators in a falls-count-anywhere brawl.

tenures.role: wrestler — Industrial Revolution; former World WAR! Tag Team Champion
tenures.source: "Nuclear WAR!fare" (7 Dec 1996): loses the World WAR! Tag Team titles to the Annihilators.

name: "Mega Daddy Kewl" MegaDiesel
caption: One half of Industrial Revolution, World WAR! Tag Team Champion by Dec 1996, losing the belts to the Annihilators in a falls-count-anywhere brawl.

tenures.role: wrestler — Industrial Revolution; former World WAR! Tag Team Champion
tenures.source: "Nuclear WAR!fare" (7 Dec 1996).

name: Venom
caption: One half of the Annihilators tag team, winning the World WAR! Tag Team titles from Industrial Revolution with a moonsault off the top of a parking-lot van.

tenures.role: wrestler — the Annihilators; World WAR! Tag Team Champion
tenures.source: "Nuclear WAR!fare" (7 Dec 1996): wins the World WAR! Tag Team titles in a falls-count-anywhere match that spills into the arena parking lot.

identity.note: "Venom" is a common gimmick name; six unrelated existing records (venom-wewf, venom-giwf, venom-oww, venom-lcw-ltd, venom-ewa, venom-cswa) share it across different feds and eras with no shared operator, roster or date evidence -- a name-only match is not a join.

name: Shinjiro Kanemoto
caption: One half of the Annihilators tag team, winning the World WAR! Tag Team titles from Industrial Revolution in a falls-count-anywhere brawl.

tenures.role: wrestler — the Annihilators; World WAR! Tag Team Champion
tenures.source: "Nuclear WAR!fare" (7 Dec 1996).

name: Matt Powers
caption: One half of Kalifornia Heat, International WAR! Tag Team Champion, retaining the titles against the All-Americans in a Texas Death match at "Nuclear WAR!fare."

tenures.role: wrestler — Kalifornia Heat; International WAR! Tag Team Champion
tenures.source: "Nuclear WAR!fare" (7 Dec 1996).

name: Danny DeLane
caption: One half of Kalifornia Heat, International WAR! Tag Team Champion, retaining the titles against the All-Americans in a Texas Death match at "Nuclear WAR!fare."

tenures.role: wrestler — Kalifornia Heat; International WAR! Tag Team Champion
tenures.source: "Nuclear WAR!fare" (7 Dec 1996).

name: Brutus "Sidewinder" Noir
caption: A vicious French brawler from the Marseille docks and one of the fed's own first World WAR! Champions, still a recurring presence through the fed's own Dec 1996 supercard.

tenures.source: "WarZone 2" (13 Oct 1995), losing to OG Gary Trent; "WarZone 3"/"Masters of War 3" (Oct 1995, billed "one of the first World War champions"); recurring through "Superstars At War! I" (Feb 1996) and the Nuclear WAR! main event (7 Dec 1996), gaining ranking points for his team's win.

name: Susan Andrews
caption: The fed's own play-by-play announcer for its Oct-Dec 1996 broadcasts, the frequent straight-woman foil to color commentator "Terrible" Terry James.

tenures.source: "Wednesday Night WAR!fare" (16 Oct 1996) through "Nuclear WAR!fare" (7 Dec 1996).

name: Inner City Firmer
caption: A shaven, tattooed brawler from Upton Park, London, and WAR!'s own second-ever World Champion, winning the title in a brutal falls-count-anywhere match that ended with a fall from the arena balcony.

tenures.source: "WarZone 2" (Season 1, 12 May 1995), losing the inaugural World Championship tournament final; wins the title itself from Brutus Noir on "WarZone 3" (Season 1, 19 May 1995); stripped of it after a hospitalization angle before "WAR!REPORT 5" and "CivilWar 1" (29 May-7 Jun 1995).

name: Johnny Thunder
caption: A high-flying wrestler from Chicago, Illinois, and WAR!'s own second-ever International War Champion, a recurring main-eventer through the fed's own first supercard.

tenures.source: "WAR!ZONE 1" (5 May 1995) debut; wins the International War Championship from Bludgeon on "WAR!TIME" (11 May 1995); retains through "WAR!REPORT 3" and "WarZone 3" before losing it to "The American" Butch Williams at NuclearWar 1 (recapped in "A Week at WAR!," 28 May 1995); loses the inaugural Jim Hellwig Cup final to Williams at "CivilWar 1" (7 Jun 1995).

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (johnny-thunder-rspwf); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

name: Bludgeon
caption: A powerhouse brawler and founding member of the Masters of War stable, and WAR!'s own first-ever International War Champion.

tenures.source: Wins the inaugural International War Championship tournament on "WAR!REPORT 2" (9 May 1995); loses it to Johnny Thunder by submission on "WAR!TIME" (11 May 1995); loses a table-match rematch on "WarZone 3" (19 May 1995).

name: "Trailboss" Mike Dallas
caption: A 7'2" wrestler managed by Mr. Kang, WAR!'s own first tag-team champion (with XL-9) and the fed's own first "Freedom" champion.

tenures.source: Co-wins WAR!'s original tag-team title alongside XL-9 at "WarZone 1" (5 May 1995); wins it outright from XL-9 on "WAR!REPORT 3" (16 May 1995), where it is immediately declared defunct in favor of a new singles "Freedom" title awarded to him; loses the vacant World Championship match to Seth Blitzspear at NuclearWar 1 (recapped in "A Week at WAR!," 28 May 1995); a double-DQ World-title challenger on "WAR!REPORT 5" (29 May 1995) and a Group 2 competitor at "CivilWar 1" (7 Jun 1995).

name: XL-9
caption: A wrestler who insists he is a robot ("self-proclaimed," per the broadcast), managed by "The Prof," and WAR!'s own first tag-team champion alongside Trailboss Mike Dallas.

tenures.source: Co-wins WAR!'s original tag-team title alongside Trailboss Mike Dallas at "WarZone 1" (5 May 1995); retains it by DQ on "WAR!TIME" (11 May 1995); loses it outright to Trailboss on "WAR!REPORT 3" (16 May 1995), where the title is immediately declared defunct.

name: The Maltese Falcon
caption: A high-flying, masked wrestler from Malta who won the Freedom Championship from "Trailboss" Mike Dallas, lost it to Bombsquad, and won it back in a cage match — the title's own busiest early stretch.

tenures.source: Debuts on "WAR!TIME" (11 May 1995); wins the Freedom title from Trailboss Mike Dallas at NuclearWar 1 (recapped in "A Week at WAR!," 28 May 1995); retains it by DQ on "WAR!REPORT 5" (29 May 1995); a Group 2 competitor at "CivilWar 1" (7 Jun 1995).

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (the-maltese-falcon-npwa); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

name: Rick "Ricky" Soal
caption: A co-broadcaster alongside "Avocado" Bob Whitely, introduced on WAR!'s own one-year anniversary supercard.

tenures.source: Co-hosts "WARATHON I" (26 April 1996) alongside "Avocado" Bob Whitely.

name: Tallyman
caption: One half of DangerZone, WAR!'s own first International WAR! Tag Team Champions.

tenures.source: As one half of DangerZone, wins the inaugural International WAR! Tag Team Championship at "CivilWar 1" (7 Jun 1995).

name: Styx
caption: One half of DangerZone, WAR!'s own first International WAR! Tag Team Champions.

tenures.source: As one half of DangerZone, wins the inaugural International WAR! Tag Team Championship at "CivilWar 1" (7 Jun 1995).

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (styx-moa); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

name: Bombsquad
caption: A recurring Season 1-2 brawler and one-time Freedom Champion, best known for his "A-Bomb" inverted powerbomb finisher and his long-running feud with the Maltese Falcon over the belt.

tenures.source: "WAR!REPORT 6" (5 Jun 1995), pinning the Maltese Falcon for the Freedom Championship; loses it back to Falcon four days later on "WarZone 6" (9 Jun 1995); recurring as an International War Championship contender through "WAR!REPORT 7" (13 Jun 1995) and into the Season 2 relaunch ("WarZone 1," 6 Oct 1995).

name: Brewster Cogburn
caption: A veteran "legend" brawler billed the fed's own first challenger for an interfed FWA/WAR! title, later winning the International War Championship outright in a vacant-title match.

tenures.source: Selected as WAR!'s own first challenger for the FWA/WAR! interfed title on "WarZone 5" (1 Jun 1995); wins the vacant International War Championship over Bombsquad on "WAR!REPORT 7" (13 Jun 1995) and retains it against Brutus Noir on "WarZone 7" (16 Jun 1995); recurring as a tag partner and rival through "Casualties of War 2" (23 Nov 1995).

identity.note: Name collision only: two other same-named entities exist in the registry (brewster-cogburn, tenures in summit-of-e-wrestling/ufws; brewster-cogburn-emwa, tenure in emwa). No shared operator, chronology or crossover evidence found in this wing's own documents; a stock cowboy-brawler gimmick name plausibly reused independently.

name: "008" Jim Bondo
caption: A recurring "Clique" member billed under the tongue-in-cheek ring name "008," twice winning the Liberty Championship across the fed's own Season 2-3 run.

tenures.source: "Superstars At War! II" (21 Feb 1996), winning the Liberty Championship from Sid Starr; retains it on "WarZone III" (4 Mar 1996); awarded the title a second time on "Superstars At War V" (15 Mar 1996) when Butch Williams hands it over on quitting WAR!.

name: Bane
caption: A masked powerhouse who won the International War Championship twice in 1996, first from Lord Byron and then from "Magnum" Biff McGriff, wrestling under successive managers King Benny, Flea and Colt McGraw.

tenures.source: Recurring from "Superstars At War IIX" (17 May 1996) through "Acts of War! — The Brawl Before the Brawl" (c. 27-28 Nov 1996); wins the International War Championship from Lord Byron at EXTINCTION `96 (28 Jun 1996) and again from "Magnum" Biff McGriff at the card immediately preceding MEGAWAR I (c. 27-28 Nov 1996).

identity.note: A stock villain-name coincidence with four other wings' own "Bane" characters (different feds, different eras, no shared operator/roster/date evidence); a name-only match is not a join.

name: Tyler Stevens
caption: "The Heartbreak Kid," a Liberty Champion three times over in the fed's own 1996 run, whose on-air heel turn and "exploding girl incident" storyline briefly put him out of action.

tenures.source: Wins the Liberty Championship from 008 Jim Bondo on "Superstars At War IV" (8 Mar 1996) and again from DeathJester on "Casualties of War III" (24 May 1996); recurring with bodyguard Venom through "Acts of War!" (22 Nov 1996).

name: T.J. "Thunder" Decan
caption: A 560-pound powerhouse recruited from NCW who won the fed's own in-house Tournament of Champions to become World WAR! Champion in late 1996, then lost the belt back to Tonnage on his first defense.

tenures.source: Debuts in the Countdown to Extinction `96 tournament (Jun 1996), which he wins; beats Tonnage in the Tournament of Champions final at "War!Mongers" (c. early Nov 1996, not itself recovered in this pull) to become World WAR! Champion, cited retrospectively in "WAR!Time" (13 Nov 1996); loses the title back to Tonnage the same night; sides with Armageddon after Seth Blitzspear relinquishes the World title.

name: StormStalker
caption: A rookie high-flyer who won the Liberty Championship from OG Gary Trent in mid-1996 and, after re-branding himself simply "The Stalker," held it into the autumn before losing it to "Dirty" Doug Simpkins.

tenures.source: Debuts in the Countdown to Extinction `96 tournament (Jun 1996); billed Liberty Champion by EXTINCTION `96 (28 Jun 1996), the title win itself not recovered; rebrands on-air from "Storm Stalker" to "The Stalker" after a chair attack on "WAR!fare" (16 Oct 1996, already served); loses the Liberty title circa 11 Nov 1996 (BattleLines, not recovered).

name: Nomad
caption: A masked Ground Zero wrestler who won the WarLord and National WAR! Championships across the fed's 1997 season, both reigns shadowed by allegations of stablemate interference.

tenures.source: Recurring as a Ground Zero member from "War!Zone" (5 May 1997, Madrid), where he wins the WarLord Championship from "Jamaican Superstar" Arron Iron by sleeperhold, through "War!Zone - OverKill" (8 Sep 1997), where he wins the National WAR! Championship from Tommy Walks-With-Thunder with Juggernaut's ringside interference.

identity.note: A stock ring-name coincidence with unrelated existing characters in other wings (a different masked "Nomad" in each); no shared operator, roster or date evidence connects them to this WAR! Ground Zero wrestler.

name: Survival
caption: A debuting Rochester, New York grappler who won the vacant WarLord Championship at Extinction '97 by taking the eight-man Helmroy Cup tournament, remaining undefeated across the reading window.

tenures.source: Debuts on "War!Zone - To Kill or be Killed" (30 May 1997, collected, not served) and wins the Helmroy Cup final over Ryan "The Intrepid" Howard at "Extinction '97 - The Oblivion" (13 Jun 1997) to claim the vacant WarLord Championship.

identity.note: An unrelated existing character, survival-rspwf, shares the ring name with no shared-operator or shared-continuity evidence recovered in this pass; flagged on the collision sheet given this wing's own documented interfed ties, for a coordinator cross-reference check rather than a merge here.

name: Tommy Walks-With-Thunder
caption: A Riverton, Wyoming wrestler billed as Native American who became the fed's first-ever National WAR! Champion in August 1997 during its relaunch under new ownership, losing the title to Nomad the following month.

tenures.source: Debuts in the 14-man battle royale on "War!Zone - All But One" (17 Aug 1997) and wins the inaugural National WAR! Championship over the Southern Man by countout on "War!Zone - Loud & Proud" (24 Aug 1997); loses the title to Nomad on "War!Zone - OverKill" (8 Sep 1997).

name: Arron Iron
caption: A singles wrestler billed the "Jamaican Superstar" who inherited the vacant WarLord Championship off-page in April 1997 and held it for roughly two weeks before losing it to Nomad.

tenures.source: Billed "current War!Lord" on "War!Zone - Death of Innocence" (22 Apr 1997, served) after T.J. "Thunder" Decan's own off-page forfeiture; loses the title to Nomad by submission on "War!Zone" (5 May 1997, already served — existing reign war-1995-warlord-r004).

identity.note: A stock ring-name coincidence with an existing entry, arron-iron-rspwf, drawn only from a 2004 RSPWF Top 200 poll placing (federation tag "WILD", no tenure of its own); no shared operator, roster or date evidence connects the two.

name: Southern Man
caption: A New Zealand-born wrestler who emerged as the "New War!" roster's own World Champion during the fed's August 1997 ownership change, then beat the "Old War!" line's own Doug Simpkins in a unification match to become the sole, undisputed World WAR! Champion — a reign cut short a week later by injury.

tenures.source: Billed the "New War!" roster's own World Champion by the fed's own August 1997 relaunch (per "THIS IS WAR! - REPORT", 30 Sep 1997, collected); beats "Dirty" Doug Simpkins by countout in a unification match on "THIS IS WAR!" (7 Oct 1997, already served) to become Undisputed World WAR! Champion; stripped of the title after an in-ring injury at "WAR!Zone - AfterMath" (11 Oct 1997, served).

name: Juggernaut
caption: A 458lb Ground Zero enforcer from Whistler, BC who arrived in the fed's own August 1997 relaunch already carrying an outside "HWA" championship as a bragging-rights prop, then won a 30-man Royal Rumble and, days later, the vacant World WAR! Championship itself.

tenures.source: A Ground Zero member interfering in two title matches the wing's own 1997 record records (the National WAR! Championship, 24 Aug and 8 Sep 1997, already served); wins a 30-man Royal Rumble on "WAR!Zone - AfterMath" (11 Oct 1997, served) to earn a World WAR! Championship shot, then wins the vacant title from Seth Blitzspear by pinfall (manager interference) on "War!Report - 20 Oct 97".

identity.note: Shares a bare ring name with an existing character in an unrelated wing, juggernaut-wewf (a 1991 WeWF World Champion); no shared operator, roster or continuity evidence connects the two — different fed, different era, six years apart.

name: "The Bullet" Ricky Revolution
caption: A Daytona Beach wrestler, managed by Sally McClane, who won the Liberty Championship in an unrecovered tournament after Sid Starr's own medical stripping and, by his own later billing, never lost it in the ring.

tenures.source: Won the vacant Liberty Championship in an unrecovered tournament between Sid Starr's own stripping (13 Jun 1997) and a 30 Sep 1997 preview describing him as champion ("THIS IS WAR! - REPORT", collected, its facts absorbed into the already-served "THIS IS WAR!" show text); billed "THE FORMER LIBERTY CHAMPION" entering a fresh title tournament on "THIS IS WAR!" (7 Oct 1997, already served), where he beats Sid Starr in the quarter-final.

identity.note: Shares a billed name with an existing character in an unrelated wing, ricky-revolution-ccw (Classic Championship Wrestling/FASW, 1996-97 tenure); no shared operator, roster or continuity evidence connects the two — a bare-name coincidence between contemporaneous but unrelated e-feds.

name: Gabrielle Whitecross
caption: Won a WAR! tournament, and by early 1998 held the EMWC World Heavyweight Championship.

tenures.source: Beats Michael Dream in the Liberty Championship tournament quarter-final on "THIS IS WAR!" (7 Oct 1997, already served); wins the tournament final over Damon "Firestarter" Curtis by submission on "War!Report - 20 Oct 97". The source text spells the name both "Gabriel" and "Gabrielle"; "Gabrielle" is used here, matching the winning result's own announcement.

name: Darkness
caption: Half of the tag team Phantasmagoria, tagging in from Terror to finish Jeff Borbone with a top-rope clothesline and pin him for the International WAR! Tag Team Championship.

tenures.source: "(WAR!) WAR!CORE" (msg_id Bcy0L6o1HoAJ, 13 Feb 1997): Greg [Addams] whips Darkness to the ropes, Frank [Addams] pulls the rope down, and Darkness "goes tumbling over," drawing the Lost Boys' disqualification. "WAR!!ZONE" (msg_id srBqTXXFcMcJ, 26 Feb 1997): Terror tags Darkness, who finishes Jeff Borbone (standing in for an injured Alan Brunswick alongside Jumbo Jim Mongol) with a top-rope clothesline ("The Final Hour") and covers for the pin, winning the International WAR! Tag Team Championship for Phantasmagoria.

name: Terror
caption: Half of the tag team Phantasmagoria, hitting the Free-Fall powerbomb on Jeff Borbone before tagging Darkness to close out the International WAR! Tag Team Championship win.

tenures.source: "WAR!!ZONE" (msg_id srBqTXXFcMcJ, 26 Feb 1997): with the International WAR! name: Greg Addams
caption: One half of the tag team the Lost Boys, billed as Lost Boy 1 before an angle by his own manager's ambusher revealed his civilian name.

tenures.source: "Lost Boys Developments" (msg_id VBly2LSIIPoJ, 28 Jun 1996): the only surviving document to reveal the Lost Boys' own civilian names, naming "Lost Boy One (Greg Addams)" directly during a crowbar ambush by Arron Iron and manager Wendy Addams. WAR!CORE" (msg_id Bcy0L6o1HoAJ, 13 Feb 1997): wrestling directly under the name, whipping Darkness to the ropes in the Lost Boys' tag title match. "War!Zone -- The AfterMath" (msg_id uTpdh5uty9AJ, 11 Oct 1997) and "THIS IS WAR!" season finale (msg_ids Ppl9MLHeWtcJ/twzderWb2qEJ/y4xVdYrxX1QJ, 7 Oct 1997): wrestling under the name in multi-man matches.

identity.note: A same-named brother pair (Greg and Frank Addams, team 'the Lost Boys', manager Wendy Addams) debuts on the held wing bwa's own 11 Sep 1997 broadcast, billed in-fiction as arriving 'from WAR! and the AWA' after 'rumors...about WAR! closing.' Tested two axes plus chronology: no operator/host/roster/title continuity connects the two wings (bwa's own founding Players Guide describes formation from merged British regional promotions, with no mention of WAR!); and the chronology CONTRADICTS rather than confirms -- war-1995's own served cards show a Greg Addams/Frank Addams/Wendy Addams 'Lost Boys' team actively wrestling and winning FOR WAR! on 7 and 11 October 1997 ("THIS IS WAR!", msg_ids Ppl9MLHeWtcJ/twzderWb2qEJ/y4xVdYrxX1QJ; "War!Zone -- The AfterMath", msg_id uTpdh5uty9AJ), weeks AFTER bwa's own bio places this character already departed and signed elsewhere (11-25 Sep 1997). war-1995 itself did not close -- its own record shows continuous operation, new-ownership relaunch and an explicitly unbroken title lineage through at least 21 Oct 1997. A same-fed appearance postdating the claimed departure is a contradicting chronology under this collection's own identity-join discipline; filed distinct rather than presumed-same pending any further document that resolves the overlap.

name: Alan Brunswick
caption: One third of the tag team the All-Americans, pinning Matt Powers to win the International WAR! Tag Team Championship before an in-fiction "soul-stealing" angle wrote him out of the following title defense.

tenures.source: "WAR!ZONE" (msg_id Sw788KKQi1QJ, 11 Feb 1997): pins Matt Powers (Kalifornia Heat) with "The Bomb" (a shooting star press) to win the International WAR! Tag Team Championship for the All-Americans, w/ Ms. America and JJM. "WAR!!ZONE" (msg_id srBqTXXFcMcJ, 26 Feb 1997): the same broadcast's own provenance records him written out of this title defense by a prior card's "soul-stealing" angle, his partners Jeff Borbone and Jumbo Jim Mongol defending in his place.

name: Jeff Borbone
caption: One third of the tag team the All-Americans, defending the International WAR! Tag Team Championship alongside Jumbo Jim Mongol before losing the titles to Phantasmagoria.

tenures.source: "WAR!!ZONE" (msg_id srBqTXXFcMcJ, 26 Feb 1997): billed "BORBONE & MONGOL w/ Ms. America" defending the International WAR! Tag Team titles for the All-Americans (standing in for the injured Alan Brunswick) against Phantasmagoria, taken the Free-Fall powerbomb from Terror before Darkness pins him with a top-rope clothesline, closing the reign.

name: Jumbo Jim Mongol
caption: One third of the tag team the All-Americans, filling in for an injured Alan Brunswick to defend the International WAR! Tag Team Championship against Phantasmagoria.

tenures.source: "WAR!!ZONE" (msg_id srBqTXXFcMcJ, 26 Feb 1997): billed "BORBONE & MONGOL w/ Ms. America" defending the International WAR! Tag Team titles for the All-Americans (standing in for the injured Alan Brunswick) against Phantasmagoria; his weight poses "a slight problem" against the double team before Phantasmagoria finishes his partner Borbone for the pin, closing the reign.

name: Wolfgang
caption: A 7-foot, 328-pound World WAR! Champion by early 1999, billed as an "angel" opposite Juggernaut's own ruthlessness before losing the title to him in a four-way at War!Zone: Beyond Hell.

tenures.source: Billed the reigning World WAR! Champion in the promotion's own 14 March 1999 rankings bulletin (13-1-0 record); pinned by Juggernaut in a four-way World WAR! Championship match on "War!Zone: Beyond Hell" (31 March 1999), ending the reign.

identity.note: Shares only the single-word ring name "Wolfgang" with three unrelated full-named characters on file (Wolfgang Einhurst, Wolfgang Von Richter, Wolfgang Rainier G.); no shared surname, operator, roster or continuity evidence connects any of them to this wing's own bare-named wrestler.

name: Blackhawk
caption: A World WAR! Championship four-way contender at War!Zone: Beyond Hell, drawn into a bitter feud after taking Wendy Addams from Arron Iron.

tenures.source: Competes in the four-way World WAR! Championship match on "War!Zone: Beyond Hell" (31 March 1999), counted out at ringside without winning the title.

identity.note: Shares only the single-word ring name "Blackhawk" with two unrelated full-named characters on file (Blackhawk McKnight, registered in two places); no shared surname, operator, roster or continuity evidence connects them.

name: "The Mangler" Ricky Deathwish
caption: A World WAR! Tag Team Champion by early 1999, teaming with Tyler Stevens to take the belts from Sid Starr and Nomad in a screwjob decided by a bribed guest referee.

tenures.role: wrestler — World WAR! Tag Team Champion
tenures.source: Billed the Liberty Champion and a World WAR! Tag Team Championship challenger in the promotion's own 14 March 1999 rankings and card preview; wins the World WAR! Tag Team Championship with Tyler Stevens from Sid Starr and Nomad on "War!Zone: Beyond Hell" (31 March 1999) after guest referee Jeff Westfall (a wrestler from another held promotion, officiating only, not competing) fast-counts the champions.

identity.note: Shares the full name "Ricky Deathwish" with an unrelated character registered in a 2003 promotion (dwf-motr); no shared operator, roster or continuity evidence, and the two records sit six years and a different fed apart.

name: "Heavy Weapons" Max Doom
caption: A War!Lord Championship contender who won the vacated title in the Brooklyn Brawl battle royal at War!Zone: Beyond Hell, throwing the last two men over the top rope to claim the belt and the $1,000,000 prize.

tenures.source: Billed a War!Lord Championship contender in the promotion's own 14 March 1999 rankings; wins the vacated War!Lord Championship in the Brooklyn Brawl over-the-top-rope battle royal on "War!Zone: Beyond Hell" (31 March 1999), eliminating Ronnie Severn and Dr. Melancholy last.

name: "The Executive" Mordecai Winchester
caption: A Boston financier-styled rulebreaker who took the WAR! Manhattan Championship in a masked-opponent swerve and used it to run the newly formed Church of Fat.

tenures.source: Wrestles Jerry Gordon to a broken-limousine draw at "Extinction '99" (22 June 1999); wins the Manhattan Championship from a masked stand-in billed as Jeff Westfall (13 September 1999) and defends it through "War!Report 4.4" (6 October 1999).

name: "The Nihilist" Ronny Ramirez
caption: A Las Vegas-based WAR!Lord Champion, accompanied to the ring by a bodyguard, who held the title through the promotion's own 1999 season before a career-threatening feud forced him out of WAR! for six months.

tenures.source: Defends the WAR!Lord Championship in a steel cage against "Heavy Weapons" Max Doom at "Extinction '99" (22 June 1999); fights Butch Williams to a double count-out draw at "War!Report 4.2" (21 September 1999), vacating the title and leaving WAR! for six months.

identity.note: Name collision only: same-named wrestlers are recorded on unrelated promotions; nothing in this wing's documents links them.

name: "Iceman" Jeff Westfall
caption: A veteran rulebreaker billed from other promotions who held the Manhattan Championship into mid-1999, cost Juggernaut a world-title defense, and later feuded with Steve Swanson.

tenures.source: Defends the Manhattan Championship on a ladder against Seth Blitzspear at "Extinction '99" (22 June 1999); interferes in the World WAR! Championship main event of "War!Report 4.0" (3 September 1999); loses to Steve Swanson at "War!Report 4.5" (13 October 1999) after manager interference.

name: "Lucky" Jim Howard
caption: WAR!'s president through the first half of 1999, known for on-air rulings against its champions before handing the office to Eric Helmroy.

tenures.source: Strips Frank Addams of the WAR!Lord Championship over a failed drug test at "War!Zone: Beyond Hell" (31 March 1999); referees the World WAR! Championship main event of "Extinction '99" (22 June 1999) after the assigned official is knocked out.

name: "Bad Seed" Ronnie Severn
caption: A volatile newcomer, claiming kinship with a famous wrestling name, whose neck injury and on-air breakdown opened WAR!'s closing 1999 supercard.

tenures.source: Debuts as a Brooklyn Brawl entrant at "War!Zone: Beyond Hell" (31 March 1999); suffers a storyline neck injury and lashes out at officials and Nick Demola in the opening angle of "Extinction '99" (22 June 1999).

name: Nick Demola
caption: A former group leader who walked out on his own stable earlier in 1999 and returned months later to confront his old running mates.

tenures.source: Returns to confront Ronnie Severn and his own former partners in the opening angle of "Extinction '99" (22 June 1999), only to be jumped by Ricky Deathwish and Jeff Westfall.

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named wrestler is recorded on an unrelated, later promotion; nothing links them.

name: Kenny B. Defeated
caption: An arrogant Minnesotan who debuted in WAR!'s September 1999 relaunch and fought through to the Liberty Championship tournament final.

tenures.source: Debuts on "War!Report 4.0" (3 September 1999); wins a Liberty title tournament semi-final at "War!Report 4.1" (13 September 1999) before losing the final to Greg Allocca at "War!Report 4.2" (21 September 1999).

name: "Playboy" Aidan Madison
caption: A high-flying rookie from West Virginia who debuted in WAR!'s September 1999 relaunch and was repeatedly targeted by Greg Allocca.

tenures.source: Debuts and wins on "War!Report 4.0" (3 September 1999), then is attacked by Greg Allocca; reaches a Liberty title tournament semi-final at "War!Report 4.1" (13 September 1999); loses a non-title match to Allocca at "War!Report 4.4" (6 October 1999).

name: "Dutch Boy" Brian Holland
caption: A power wrestler from Rhode Island who returned to WAR! for its September 1999 relaunch in an on-again, off-again feud with Machinehead.

tenures.source: Returns against Machinehead on "War!Report 4.0" (3 September 1999) and again at "War!Report 4.1" (13 September 1999), winning the rematch; loses to Paul Novak and to American Patriot in October.

name: Machinehead
caption: A fan-favorite power wrestler from Washington, D.C. who returned for WAR!'s September 1999 relaunch in a running feud with "Dutch Boy" Brian Holland.

tenures.source: Defeats Brian Holland on "War!Report 4.0" (3 September 1999); loses the rematch at "War!Report 4.1" (13 September 1999); loses to "Godly" Ken Davison at "War!Report 4.2" (21 September 1999) and is eliminated from the battle royal at "War!Report 4.5" (13 October 1999).

name: Paul Novak
caption: An 18-year-old rookie from Memphis, fresh from T.J. Decan's wrestling school, whose in-ring debut season carried him from a nervous run-in to a Liberty title shot as a member of Ground Zero.

tenures.source: Costs Ronny Ramirez his match on "War!Report 4.0" (3 September 1999); records his first win over Brian Holland at "War!Report 4.2" (21 September 1999); wrestles for Ground Zero against the Church of Fat at "War!Report 4.4" (6 October 1999); challenges Greg Allocca for the Liberty Championship at "War!Report 4.5" (13 October 1999).

name: "Superstar" Brad Hawk
caption: A Liberty Championship tournament semi-finalist during WAR!'s September 1999 relaunch, later beaten on his own return by a debuting Corporal Nobbs.

tenures.source: Wins a Liberty title tournament semi-final at "War!Report 4.1" (13 September 1999); loses to debuting Corporal Nobbs at "War!Report 4.2" (21 September 1999).

name: "Brutal" Brian Floyd
caption: An Oklahoman brawler who fought through WAR!'s September 1999 relaunch, disqualifying "Iceman" Jeff Westfall in one memorable finish before his run wound down that autumn.

tenures.source: Loses a Liberty title tournament semi-final at "War!Report 4.1" (13 September 1999); wins by disqualification over Jeff Westfall at "War!Report 4.2" (21 September 1999); fights The Golden Boy to a double count-out at "War!Report 4.4" (6 October 1999) and is eliminated from the battle royal at "War!Report 4.5" (13 October 1999).

caption: A masked wrestler who impersonated Jeff Westfall in a Manhattan Championship match and lost the title without the real champion ever setting foot in the ring.

tenures.source: Wrestles Mordecai Winchester for the Manhattan Championship at "War!Report 4.1" (13 September 1999) disguised as Jeff Westfall; unmasked as an impostor after losing the title.

name: "Godly" Ken Davison
caption: A debuting wrestler who scored a string of upset wins during WAR!'s September 1999 relaunch, including a submission win over a former World Champion.

tenures.source: Debuts with a win over Machinehead at "War!Report 4.2" (21 September 1999); referees an elimination tag match at "War!Report 4.4" (6 October 1999); beats American Patriot by submission at "War!Report 4.5" (13 October 1999).

name: Corporal Nobbs
caption: A military-trained debutant, billed as Lance F. Nobbs, whose hardcore style carried him from a rookie upset win to victory in a thirteen-man battle royal.

tenures.source: Debuts with a win over Brad Hawk at "War!Report 4.2" (21 September 1999); submits Jerry Gordon at "War!Report 4.4" (6 October 1999); wins the battle royal at "War!Report 4.5" (13 October 1999).

name: Dain Jerrus
caption: A brash newcomer who declared himself better than WAR!'s entire roster and set his sights on three championships at once.

tenures.source: Debuts with a win over Rico Zanders at "War!Report 4.4" (6 October 1999); is eliminated from the battle royal at "War!Report 4.5" (13 October 1999) after declaring he would win it.

name: "Ice Cold" Steve Swanson
caption: A returning wrestler, previously asked to leave WAR!, who came back in October 1999 with a manager and a grudge, forming Ground Zero alongside Paul Novak.

tenures.source: Returns to WAR! for the elimination tag match at "War!Report 4.4" (6 October 1999) as part of Ground Zero; defeats Jeff Westfall with his manager's help at "War!Report 4.5" (13 October 1999).

name: Dynamyte
caption: A one-man wrecking crew from Miami with his sights on the World Championship, twice held to a draw or defeated by Manhattan Champion Mordecai Winchester.

tenures.source: Fights Seth Blitzspear to a double count-out at "War!Report 4.4" (6 October 1999); loses a non-title match to Manhattan Champion Mordecai Winchester at "War!Report 4.5" (13 October 1999).

name: Mistress Sarah
caption: Steve Swanson's manager, whose ringside interference turned his October 1999 return match.

tenures.source: Accompanies Steve Swanson and knocks out Jeff Westfall with his own baseball bat behind the referee's back at "War!Report 4.5" (13 October 1999).

name: "Hard" Harry Who
caption: A small but hard-hitting jobber who lost to Kenny B. Defeated on WAR!'s September 1999 relaunch and was eliminated early from that October's battle royal.

tenures.source: Loses to Kenny B. Defeated on "War!Report 4.0" (3 September 1999); eliminated early from the battle royal at "War!Report 4.5" (13 October 1999).

name: Super Heavy Stan
caption: WAR!'s biggest and meanest showcase wrestler, tapped out by "Playboy" Aidan Madison on the promotion's September 1999 relaunch show.

tenures.source: Loses to "Playboy" Aidan Madison by submission on "War!Report 4.0" (3 September 1999).

name: The Mad Goat
caption: A costumed novelty entrant in WAR!'s September 1999 Liberty Championship tournament, managed to the ring and eliminated from the battle royal a month later.

tenures.source: Loses a Liberty title tournament semi-final to Greg Allocca by count-out at "War!Report 4.1" (13 September 1999); eliminated early from the battle royal at "War!Report 4.5" (13 October 1999).

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (mad-goat-nccw-utm-1998); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

name: "Hardcore Kid" Rico Zanders
caption: A low-profile brawler who lost his WAR! debut to Dain Jerrus and was eliminated early from the following week's battle royal.

tenures.source: Loses to Dain Jerrus at "War!Report 4.4" (6 October 1999); eliminated early from the battle royal at "War!Report 4.5" (13 October 1999).

name: The Golden Boy
caption: A flamboyant debutant who fought "Brutal" Brian Floyd to a double count-out and was eliminated from the following week's battle royal.

tenures.source: Debuts against "Brutal" Brian Floyd in a double count-out at "War!Report 4.4" (6 October 1999); eliminated from the battle royal at "War!Report 4.5" (13 October 1999).
